nodes.description: Validate the input is a UUID matching support_tickets.id. If it is not a UUID, ask for the ticket ID rather than guessing — the skill is explicit about not guessing here. A ticket already `resolved` or `closed` needs no triage.

Invoke the Helpdesk agent (cli: `run helpdesk --input {action:'triage', ticketId}`). It loads customer, plan, prior tickets and policy KB, then returns: intent (plan-limit | billing | refund | bug-report | how-to), confidence 0.0-1.0, draftReply, recommendedAction, citedPolicySources.

Route on the agent's recommendedAction and confidence. The skill's documented rule: confidence < 0.6, or an action of `escalate` or `refund`, means the agent has already opened an hil_escalations row and set the ticket to awaiting_human — that path is not a draft-and-send path.

RED zone: the Helpdesk agent NEVER sends email — a human reviewer must approve the draft. Surface the draft reply verbatim plus its cited policy sources, and stop. Only an explicit human approval of this exact draft permits SEND_REPLY. Same structural gate as Chapter 1's outbound-email gate; the runner's DEFAULT_GATED_NODE_IDS covers this node id automatically.
Reachable only through HIC_APPROVAL_GATE. The reviewer's action: POST /api/v1/support/tickets/:id/send. The graph does not send on its own — it records that the approved send happened.
Reply sent; awaiting customer response. A follow-up reply is a NEW draft and re-enters TRIAGE then HIC_APPROVAL_GATE — never a resend on the prior approval.

An hil_escalations row exists and the ticket is awaiting_human (low confidence, refund, or explicit escalate). Surface the escalation ID and reason to the reviewer. Terminal for the agent — a human owns the ticket from here.
recommendedAction is `resolve` with no outbound reply needed (e.g. the issue self-resolved or was a duplicate). No approval gate applies because nothing leaves the building.
Agent invocation failed, or the send call errored. Diagnose (bad ticket ID, agent timeout, delivery failure) and retry the triage rather than fabricating a reply.
Terminal for this run — ticket deferred, out of scope, or already closed on arrival.
